claim: The neurotransmitter:sodium symporters (NSSs) are secondary active transporters that couple the reuptake of substrate to the symport of one or two sodium ions.
source: The neurotransmitter:sodium symporters (NSSs) are secondary active transporters that couple the reuptake of substrate to the symport of one or two sodium ions.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about NSS proteins that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: One bound Na+ (Na1) contributes to the substrate binding in NSSs.
source: One bound Na+ (Na1) contributes to the substrate binding, while the other Na+ (Na2) is thought to be involved in the conformational transition of the NSS.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge about NSS function and is cited in the literature.

claim: The Na2 sodium ion is thought to be involved in the conformational transition of the NSS.
source: One bound Na+ (Na1) contributes to the substrate binding, while the other Na+ (Na2) is thought to be involved in the conformational transition of the NSS.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the role of Na2 based on existing knowledge.

claim: The serotonin transporter (SERT) couples substrate uptake to the antiport of K+.
source: Two NSS members, the serotonin transporter (SERT) and the Drosophila dopamine transporter (dDAT), also couple substrate uptake to the antiport of K+ by a largely undefined mechanism.
evidence: This is supported by citations in the manuscript and established knowledge.

claim: The Drosophila dopamine transporter (dDAT) couples substrate uptake to the antiport of K+.
source: Two NSS members, the serotonin transporter (SERT) and the Drosophila dopamine transporter (dDAT), also couple substrate uptake to the antiport of K+ by a largely undefined mechanism.
evidence: This is supported by citations in the manuscript and established knowledge.

claim: The mechanism by which SERT and dDAT couple substrate uptake to K+ antiport is largely undefined.
source: Two NSS members, the serotonin transporter (SERT) and the Drosophila dopamine transporter (dDAT), also couple substrate uptake to the antiport of K+ by a largely undefined mechanism.
evidence: This statement acknowledges the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The bacterial NSS homologue LeuT binds K+.
source: We have previously shown that the bacterial NSS homologue, LeuT, also binds K+, and could therefore serve as a model protein for the exploration of K+ binding in NSS proteins.
evidence: This is supported by previous work by the authors, as indicated by the citation.

claim: LeuT can serve as a model protein for the exploration of K+ binding in NSS proteins.
source: We have previously shown that the bacterial NSS homologue, LeuT, also binds K+, and could therefore serve as a model protein for the exploration of K+ binding in NSS proteins.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that LeuT binds K+ and is a bacterial homologue of NSS proteins.

claim: K+ binding to LeuT is specific and saturable.
source: K+ binding was specific and saturable.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from radioligand binding assays and tmFRET experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Radioligand binding assays and tmFRET yielded similar K+ affinities for LeuT.
source: Both radioligand binding assays and transition metal ion FRET (tmFRET) yielded similar K+ affinities for LeuT.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing the two methods presented in the manuscript.

claim: Intra-vesicular K+ dose-dependently increased the transport velocity of [3H]alanine by LeuT reconstituted into proteoliposomes.
source: LeuT reconstituted into proteoliposomes showed that intra-vesicular K+ dose-dependently increased the transport velocity of [3H]alanine, whereas extra-vesicular K+ had no apparent effect.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from transport assays with reconstituted LeuT.

claim: Extra-vesicular K+ had no apparent effect on [3H]alanine transport by LeuT reconstituted into proteoliposomes.
source: LeuT reconstituted into proteoliposomes showed that intra-vesicular K+ dose-dependently increased the transport velocity of [3H]alanine, whereas extra-vesicular K+ had no apparent effect.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from transport assays with reconstituted LeuT.

claim: K+ binding induced a LeuT conformation distinct from the Na+- and substrate-bound conformation.
source: K+ binding induced a LeuT conformation distinct from the Na+- and substrate-bound conformation.
evidence: This is supported by tmFRET data showing different conformational states.

claim: Conservative mutations of the Na1 site residues affected the binding of Na+ and K+ to different degrees.
source: Conservative mutations of the Na1 site residues affected the binding of Na+ and K+ to different degrees.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from radioligand binding assays with mutant LeuT proteins.

claim: The Na1 site mutation N27Q caused a >10-fold decrease in K+ affinity.
source: The Na1 site mutation N27Q caused a >10-fold decrease in K+ affinity but at the same time a ~3-fold increase in Na+ affinity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from radioligand binding assays with the N27Q mutant.

claim: The Na1 site mutation N27Q caused a ~3-fold increase in Na+ affinity.
source: The Na1 site mutation N27Q caused a >10-fold decrease in K+ affinity but at the same time a ~3-fold increase in Na+ affinity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from radioligand binding assays with the N27Q mutant.

claim: K+ binding to LeuT modulates substrate transport.
source: Together, the results suggest that K+ binding to LeuT modulates substrate transport and that the K+ affinity and selectivity for LeuT is sensitive to mutations in the Na1 site, pointing toward the Na1 site as a candidate site for facilitating the interaction with K+ in some NSSs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing effects of K+ on transport velocity.

claim: The K+ affinity and selectivity for LeuT is sensitive to mutations in the Na1 site.
source: Together, the results suggest that K+ binding to LeuT modulates substrate transport and that the K+ affinity and selectivity for LeuT is sensitive to mutations in the Na1 site, pointing toward the Na1 site as a candidate site for facilitating the interaction with K+ in some NSSs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing differential effects of Na1 site mutations on K+ binding.

claim: The Na1 site is a candidate site for facilitating the interaction with K+ in some NSSs.
source: Together, the results suggest that K+ binding to LeuT modulates substrate transport and that the K+ affinity and selectivity for LeuT is sensitive to mutations in the Na1 site, pointing toward the Na1 site as a candidate site for facilitating the interaction with K+ in some NSSs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing effects of Na1 site mutations on K+ binding.

claim: The monoamine transporters (MATs) include the dopamine transporter (DAT), the norepinephrine transporter (NET), and the serotonin transporter (SERT).
source: Of pronounced interest to neuropharmacology is the subclass of monoamine transporters (MATs), including the dopamine transporter (DAT), the norepinephrine transporter (NET), and the serotonin transporter (SERT), which are molecular targets for a range of psychopharmaceuticals, including drugs against depression, anxiety, neuropathic pain, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and narcolepsy (Kristensen et al., 2011; Aggarwal and Mortensen, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: MATs are molecular targets for a range of psychopharmaceuticals, including drugs against depression, anxiety, neuropathic pain, ADHD, and narcolepsy.
source: Of pronounced interest to neuropharmacology is the subclass of monoamine transporters (MATs), including the dopamine transporter (DAT), the norepinephrine transporter (NET), and the serotonin transporter (SERT), which are molecular targets for a range of psychopharmaceuticals, including drugs against depression, anxiety, neuropathic pain, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and narcolepsy (Kristensen et al., 2011; Aggarwal and Mortensen, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: MATs are targets for psychostimulant drugs of abuse, such as cocaine and amphetamine.
source: They are also targets for psychostimulant drugs of abuse, such as cocaine and amphetamine (Jayanthi and Ramamoorthy, 2005; Di Giovanni et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: LeuT is a hydrophobic amino acid transporter originating from the thermophile bacterium Aquifex aeolicus.
source: The NSS member LeuT, a hydrophobic amino acid transporter originating from the thermophile bacterium Aquifex aeolicus, was the first NSS for which the structure solved (Yamashita et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by a citation.

claim: LeuT was the first NSS for which the structure was solved.
source: The NSS member LeuT, a hydrophobic amino acid transporter originating from the thermophile bacterium Aquifex aeolicus, was the first NSS for which the structure solved (Yamashita et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by a citation.

claim: LeuT has served as a structural and mechanistic model for NSS proteins.
source: LeuT has served as a structural and mechanistic model for NSS proteins (Yamashita et al., 2005; Loland, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: All NSS proteins are thought to share the LeuT-fold structure.
source: All NSS proteins are thought to share the LeuT-fold structure, comprising 10 transmembrane (TM) segments ordered in a pseudo-symmetry in the plane of the membrane between the first and the second five TMs.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field based on structural studies.

claim: The LeuT-fold structure comprises 10 transmembrane (TM) segments ordered in a pseudo-symmetry in the plane of the membrane between the first and the second five TMs.
source: All NSS proteins are thought to share the LeuT-fold structure, comprising 10 transmembrane (TM) segments ordered in a pseudo-symmetry in the plane of the membrane between the first and the second five TMs.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field based on structural studies.

claim: The LeuT-fold is mostly followed by two C-terminal TMs.
source: The LeuT-fold is mostly followed by two C-terminal TMs.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field based on structural studies.

claim: Comparing the available structures stabilized in different states of the transport cycle suggests an overall similar transport mechanism, substantiating LeuT as a valid model protein.
source: Comparing the available structures stabilized in different states of the transport cycle suggests an overall similar transport mechanism, substantiating LeuT as a valid model protein (Krishnamurthy and Gouaux, 2012; Wang et al., 2015; Yang and Gouaux, 2021; Shahsavar et al., 2021; Motiwala et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural comparisons, supported by citations.

claim: The substrate binding site in LeuT is located halfway through the core of the protein.
source: The substrate binding site is located halfway through the core of the protein and consists of coordinating residues from TM1, -3, -6, and -8 (Yamashita et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge based on structural studies, supported by a citation.

claim: The substrate binding site in LeuT consists of coordinating residues from TM1, -3, -6, and -8.
source: The substrate binding site is located halfway through the core of the protein and consists of coordinating residues from TM1, -3, -6, and -8 (Yamashita et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge based on structural studies, supported by a citation.

claim: The substrate binding site in LeuT is flanked by two Na+ binding sites, Na1 and Na2.
source: It is flanked by two Na+ binding sites, Na1 and Na2.
evidence: This is established knowledge based on structural studies.

claim: The location and the residues forming the Na1 and Na2 sites are quite conserved between LeuT and the MATs.
source: The location and the residues forming the Na1 and Na2 sites are quite conserved between LeuT and the MATs.
evidence: This is established knowledge based on structural comparisons.

claim: In the Na1 site, only one of the four coordinating residues differ by a serine to threonine substitution between LeuT and MATs.
source: In the Na1 site, only one of the four coordinating residues differ by a serine to threonine substitution.
evidence: This is established knowledge based on structural comparisons.

claim: In the Na2 site, two of the five residues are substituted between LeuT and MATs.
source: In the Na2 site, two of the five residues are substituted between LeuT and MATs.
evidence: This is established knowledge based on structural comparisons.

claim: A conserved feature shaping the Na+ binding sites is the helical unwinding in TM1 and TM6, which exposes backbone-carbonyl oxygen atoms to partake in the ion coordination.
source: A conserved feature shaping the Na+ binding sites is the helical unwinding in TM1 and TM6, which exposes backbone-carbonyl oxygen atoms to partake in the ion coordination (Yamashita et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge based on structural studies, supported by a citation.

claim: In LeuT, the Na1 ion is coordinated by the carboxyl-group of the substrate.
source: In LeuT, the Na1 ion is also coordinated by the carboxyl-group of the substrate, yielding substrate binding highly Na+-dependent (Yamashita et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge based on structural studies, supported by a citation.

claim: The coordination of the Na1 ion by the carboxyl-group of the substrate yields substrate binding highly Na+-dependent in LeuT.
source: In LeuT, the Na1 ion is also coordinated by the carboxyl-group of the substrate, yielding substrate binding highly Na+-dependent (Yamashita et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations, supported by a citation.

claim: The sodium gradient across the cell membrane is essential for driving substrate uptake in NSS proteins through occupation of the Na+ sites.
source: The sodium gradient across the cell membrane is essential for driving substrate uptake in NSS proteins through occupation of the Na+ sites.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of NSS proteins.

claim: Serotonin uptake by SERT was accelerated by an outward-directed K+ gradient.
source: In addition, it has for long been recognized that SERT antiports K+ as studies have shown that serotonin uptake was accelerated by an outward-directed K+ gradient (Nelson and Rudnick, 1979).
evidence: This is established knowledge based on previous studies, supported by a citation.

claim: K+ antiport was suggested to increase the rate of the return step in SERT, which is thought to be the rate-limiting step of the transport cycle.
source: Consequently, K+ antiport was suggested to increase the rate of the return step, which is thought to be the rate-limiting step of the transport cycle (Hasenhuetl et al., 2016; Fitzgerald et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: Cryo-EM reconstruction of SERT obtained in KCl revealed an inward-open conformation.
source: Cryo-EM reconstruction of SERT obtained in KCl revealed an inward-open conformation, suggesting this to be the most prevalent structure with KCl (Yang and Gouaux, 2021).
evidence: This is based on structural data from a cited study.

claim: The inward-open conformation is suggested to be the most prevalent structure of SERT with KCl.
source: Cryo-EM reconstruction of SERT obtained in KCl revealed an inward-open conformation, suggesting this to be the most prevalent structure with KCl (Yang and Gouaux, 2021).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural data from a cited study.

claim: The resolution of the cryo-EM structure of SERT in KCl did not allow unambiguous identification of densities for bound ions.
source: The resolution of this structure, however, did not allow unambiguous identification of densities for bound ions.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the structural data from a cited study.

claim: The location of the K+ binding site in SERT remains unknown.
source: Thus, while the conformational details of the K+-bound state of SERT are emerging, the location of the K+ binding site remains unknown and the antiport mechanism not fully understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The K+ antiport mechanism in SERT is not fully understood.
source: Thus, while the conformational details of the K+-bound state of SERT are emerging, the location of the K+ binding site remains unknown and the antiport mechanism not fully understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: K+ is antiported by DAT from Drosophila melanogaster (dDAT) by a mechanism that shares similarities with K+ antiport in SERT.
source: We have shown that K+ is antiported also by DAT from Drosophila melanogaster (dDAT) by a mechanism that shares similarities with K+ antiport in SERT (Schmidt et al., 2022).
evidence: This is based on previous work by the authors, supported by a citation.

claim: LeuT interacts with K+ and the binding favors an outward-closed conformation.
source: Previously, we have reported that LeuT interacts with K+ and that the binding favors an outward-closed conformation (Billesbølle et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on previous work by the authors, supported by a citation.

claim: Intra-vesicular K+ increased the concentrative capacity of [3H]alanine by LeuT, possibly by decreasing substrate efflux.
source: Intra-vesicular K+ also increased the concentrative capacity of [3H]alanine by LeuT, possibly by decreasing substrate efflux, but the details of K+'s interaction with LeuT were not fully explored (Billesbølle et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on previous work by the authors, with speculation about the mechanism, supported by a citation.

claim: Na+ promoted the binding of [3H]leucine to LeuT with an EC50 for Na+ of 7.7 mM.
source: Na+ promoted the binding of [3H]leucine to LeuT with an EC50 for Na+ of 7.7 mM, in line with previous studies (Zhao et al., 2011; Shi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the current study and is consistent with previous studies.

claim: In the presence of K+, the EC50 for Na+-mediated [3H]leucine binding to LeuT right-shifted while the Bmax remained unchanged.
source: In the presence of K+, however, the EC50 right-shifted while the Bmax remained unchanged, consistent with a competitive mechanism of inhibition between Na+ and K+ as suggested previously (Billesbølle et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the current study.

claim: The right-shift in EC50 for Na+ in the presence of K+ is consistent with a competitive mechanism of inhibition between Na+ and K+.
source: In the presence of K+, however, the EC50 right-shifted while the Bmax remained unchanged, consistent with a competitive mechanism of inhibition between Na+ and K+ as suggested previously (Billesbølle et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and is consistent with previous work.

claim: K+ dose-dependently displaced [3H]leucine binding to LeuT with an IC50 for K+ of 235 [225; 243] mM.
source: Displacement of [3H]leucine binding by K+ is concentration-dependent, with an IC50 for K+ of 235 [225; 243] mM (mean [s.e.m. interval]) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from radioligand binding assays shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The displacement of [3H]leucine by K+ was not caused by artifacts originating from high total salt concentrations.
source: To ensure that the displacement of [3H]leucine by K+ was not caused by artifacts originating from the high total salt concentrations (1.6 M), we repeated the displacement assay with a total ionic strength of 208 mM salt using either Ch+ or N-methyl-D-glucamine (NMDG+), both of which are inert to LeuT, as counter ions. Again, K+ dose-dependently displaced [3H]leucine binding with an inhibition constant not significantly different from that measured in the high salt conditions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from control experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The saturable, ionic strength-independent displacement of [3H]leucine binding by K+ is indicative of a specific, low affinity K+ binding site in LeuT.
source: Although the approach is indirect with respect to K+, this saturable, ionic strength-independent displacement of [3H]leucine binding is indicative of a specific, low affinity K+ binding site in LeuT.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing saturable and ionic strength-independent displacement.

claim: The tmFRET method relies on the distance-dependent quenching of a cysteine-conjugated fluorophore (FRET donor) by a transition metal (FRET acceptor), here Ni2+, coordinated to an engineered α-helical His-X3-His site.
source: This method relies on the distance-dependent quenching of a cysteine-conjugated fluorophore (FRET donor) by a transition metal (FRET acceptor), here Ni2+, coordinated to an engineered α-helical His-X3-His site (Taraska et al., 2009a).
evidence: This is a description of the tmFRET method, supported by a citation.

claim: In LeuT, the His-X3-His site was inserted in extracellular loop (EL)4a (A313H-A317H) and a cysteine at the top of TM10 (K398C) was labeled with fluorescein-5-maleimide (F5M).
source: In LeuT, we have inserted the His-X3-His site in extracellular loop (EL)4a (A313H-A317H) and a cysteine at the top of TM10 (K398C) that is labeled with fluorescein-5-maleimide (F5M).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design for the tmFRET construct.

claim: The distance between the FRET probes in LeuT changes upon opening and closing of the extracellular gate.
source: The distance between these FRET probes changes upon opening and closing of the extracellular gate in LeuT (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The LeuT A313H-A317H-K398F5M construct (LeuTtmFRET) retains WT-like activity with respect to ligand binding affinities.
source: Importantly, this construct, LeuT A313H-A317H-K398F5M (from here and on named LeuTtmFRET), retains WT activity with respect to ligand binding affinities (Billesbølle et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on previous characterization of the construct, supported by a citation.

claim: Changes in tmFRET intensity is a conformational readout for both ion and ligand binding to LeuT.
source: Accordingly, changes in tmFRET intensity is a conformational readout for both ion and ligand binding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the design and validation of the tmFRET construct.

claim: The Ni2+ affinity for the His-X3-His site is increased ~3-fold when Na+ or K+ is added to LeuT relative to NMDG+.
source: The Ni2+ affinity for the His-X3-His site is increased ~3-fold when Na+ or K+ is added to LeuT relative to NMDG+.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from tmFRET experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The increased Ni2+ affinity for the His-X3-His site when Na+ or K+ is added indicates that both Na+ and K+ bind and stabilize LeuT, including the His-X3-His motif, whereas NMDG+ does not.
source: This indicates that both Na+ and K+ bind and stabilize LeuT, including the His-X3-His motif, whereas NMDG+ does not.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing increased Ni2+ affinity.

claim: K+ uniquely stabilizes a high FRET state in LeuT, suggesting a shift in the conformational equilibrium of the transporter toward an outward-closed state by K+.
source: The FRET efficiencies at saturating Ni2+ concentrations reflect the average distance between the FRET probes and showed that K+ uniquely stabilizes a high FRET state, suggesting a shift in the conformational equilibrium of the transporter toward an outward-closed state by K+ (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from tmFRET experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Rb+ stabilized a more outward-closed state in LeuT relative to that in NMDG+.
source: Interestingly, applying Rb+, a cation often seen to be able to substitute for K+ in biological systems, also stabilized a more outward-closed state relative to that in NMDG+.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from tmFRET experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The FRET efficiency in the Na+/leucine-bound state was decreased relative to that in the Na+-bound state, suggesting a, on average, more open-to-out state when adding leucine.
source: The FRET efficiency in the Na+/leucine-bound state was decreased relative to that in the Na+-bound state, suggesting a, on average, more open-to-out state when adding leucine.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from tmFRET experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: LeuT adopts a more conformationally restricted equilibrium upon binding of leucine relative to that with Na+ alone.
source: We speculate that LeuT adopts a more conformationally restricted equilibrium upon binding of leucine relative to that with Na+ alone, and that this is reflected in a lower FRET efficiency (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental data and theoretical considerations shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Alanine binding allows a higher degree of conformational freedom in LeuT than leucine binding.
source: This is also in line with the observation that alanine gives rise to a higher FRET efficiency than leucine (Figure 2B) as alanine binding allows a higher degree of conformational freedom in the transporter (Zhao et al., 2011; Calugareanu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from tmFRET experiments and previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: The EC50 for K+ binding to apo state LeuT determined by tmFRET is 183 [176; 189] mM.
source: To estimate the affinity for K+ to apo state LeuT, we recorded the FRET efficiencies for LeuTtmFRET incubated with Ni2+ in increasing concentrations of K+ (Figure 2C). We observed an increase in FRET as a function of K+ yielding an EC50 of 183 [176; 189] mM, in line with the affinity determined by K+-dependent displacement of Na+ and [3H]leucine (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from tmFRET experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The EC50 for K+ determined by tmFRET is in line with the affinity determined by K+-dependent displacement of Na+ and [3H]leucine.
source: We observed an increase in FRET as a function of K+ yielding an EC50 of 183 [176; 189] mM, in line with the affinity determined by K+-dependent displacement of Na+ and [3H]leucine (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental data from two different methods.

claim: The EC50 for K+ determined by tmFRET is in line with the affinity from the Schild analysis performed previously.
source: This EC50 is also in line with the affinity from the Schild analysis performed previously (Billesbølle et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental data from the current study with previous work, supported by a citation.

claim: Rb+ induced a conformational response in LeuT resembling that of K+, suggesting that Rb+ can substitute for K+ although with a lower apparent affinity.
source: While Na+ did not impose major conformational changes, we found that also Rb+ induced a conformational response resembling that of K+, suggesting that Rb+ can indeed substitute for K+ although with a lower apparent affinity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from tmFRET experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The high salt concentrations did not affect the intrinsic fluorescence properties of the fluorophore.
source: Of note, the high salt concentrations did not affect the intrinsic fluorescence properties of the fluorophore, validating that the responses to titration of the ions were direct results of conformational changes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by control experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The responses to titration of the ions in tmFRET experiments were direct results of conformational changes.
source: Of note, the high salt concentrations did not affect the intrinsic fluorescence properties of the fluorophore, validating that the responses to titration of the ions were direct results of conformational changes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an inference based on control experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The effect of K+ on Na+-dependent [3H]leucine binding and the tmFRET data support the existence of a specific K+ binding site in LeuT.
source: Along with the effect of K+ on Na+-dependent [3H]leucine binding, this finding supports the existence of a specific K+ binding site in LeuT, and that K+ binding to this site induces an outward-closed conformation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined experimental data from radioligand binding and tmFRET experiments.

claim: K+ binding to LeuT induces an outward-closed conformation.
source: Along with the effect of K+ on Na+-dependent [3H]leucine binding, this finding supports the existence of a specific K+ binding site in LeuT, and that K+ binding to this site induces an outward-closed conformation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined experimental data from radioligand binding and tmFRET experiments.

claim: Proteoliposomes containing K+ displayed a 2.5-fold increase in concentrative capacity compared to those containing Cs+ or NMDG+.
source: Interestingly, proteoliposomes containing K+ displayed a 2.5-fold increase in concentrative capacity compared to those containing Cs+ or NMDG+ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from transport assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Table 1.

claim: The concentrative capacity with Rb+ was similar to that with K+, indicating that Rb+ can functionally substitute for K+.
source: The concentrative capacity with Rb+ was similar to that with K+, indicating that Rb+ can functionally substitute for K+.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from transport assays.

claim: K+ and Rb+ are not obligate for LeuT transport, but add a concentrative potential for accumulation of alanine in addition to that obtained solely by the Na+ gradient.
source: These data suggest that K+, and Rb+, are not obligate for LeuT transport, but add a concentrative potential for accumulation of alanine in addition to that obtained solely by the Na+ gradient.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from transport assays.

claim: The Km for [3H]alanine in vesicles containing K+ was 1.8±0.4 µM.
source: The Km for [3H]alanine in vesicles containing K+ was 1.8±0.4 µM, and it was not significantly different upon substitution of intra-vesicular K+ with NMDG+, Cs+, or Rb+ (Figure 3C and Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from transport assays shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The Km for [3H]alanine was not significantly different upon substitution of intra-vesicular K+ with NMDG+, Cs+, or Rb+.
source: The Km for [3H]alanine in vesicles containing K+ was 1.8±0.4 µM, and it was not significantly different upon substitution of intra-vesicular K+ with NMDG+, Cs+, or Rb+ (Figure 3C and Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from transport assays shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The Vmax for [3H]alanine uptake was not significantly different between NMDG+- and Cs+-containing proteoliposomes.
source: The Vmax for [3H]alanine uptake was not significantly different between NMDG+- and Cs+-containing proteoliposomes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from transport assays shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The Vmax for [3H]alanine uptake increased 2.5- to 3-fold when NMDG+ was substituted with Rb+ or K+.
source: In contrast, the Vmax increased 2.5- to 3-fold when NMDG+ was substituted with Rb+ or K+.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from transport assays shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The increased uptake rate by K+ could originate from increases in the rates of certain steps in the transport cycle, from a decrease in [3H]alanine efflux, or a combination of both.
source: The increased uptake rate could originate from increases in the rates of certain steps in the transport cycle, from a decrease in [3H]alanine efflux, or a combination of both.
